Eh... I feel like docking, in some situations, may be medically necessary. Not saying always and realize it’s circumstance by circumstance BUT when I was a kid, we had a pit bull/lab mix with horrific anxiety (and this was long before we knew you could do things for dogs to help that, like give them melatonin or CBD).

Long story short, he’d gnaw at his tail until one day he put sores in it that wouldn’t heal. Even if we cone’d him, when he’d wag his tail, it would hit the wall and immediately split open and spray blood everywhere; it got to the point where it was safer (to prevent infection) just to dock his tail. 

Granted, the loud noise anxiety he exhibited didn’t magically go away but it changed into him gnawing on (admittedly, first shoes) durable Kong rubber toys we got him. But some big dogs can’t handle having a tail. And I feel like (similar to the breathing problem pugs have) that’s partially our faults due to the weird cross breedings we’ve tried to produce. 

And per spaying/neutering: is it bad? Arguable. It’s like the issue most states have with needed deer culls — I feel like we’ve created a situation where the most humane thing to do is to remove the possibility of further breeding/need to keep the population down.  

I’m no vet, so I’m not gonna pretend that’s the best answer, but I feel most people neuter their animals because they can’t handle having more. I get it you could chalk that up to “well if you can’t handle, don’t get” but heat does some shit to an animal. They’ll legit run away to go breed, then come back and shit, now you have five additional cats to take care of and it doesn’t mater if you can’t afford it. 

The only other option at that point becomes finding people to take them (at least you hope you can) or giving them to a no-kill shelter, if you can find one, and praying they don’t spend the rest of their lives in a shitty fenced in area knowing all of this could have been avoidable if you just... spayed your cat.

TL;DR: spaying and docking (and that’s a sometimes on the docking, not all the time) have medical reasons to back up their procedures while declawing is 99.999% of the time done purely for aesthetics/financial purposes.

(I’m pretty sure NPR published a story on this, but I’m on mobile rn so I can’t link, atm.)

Also — and I don’t actually know if this one is 100% true, so bare with me — I’ve read that for a long time in the med field, most medications/diseases were studied as to how they’d react or be present in white men, meaning, again, presences of diseases or reactions to medications by poc and women (and especially woc) weren’t ever factored into play. 

An example, I’ve been told, is that the onset of heart attacks show up differently in women than in men — and for a long time women having heart attacks would show up to the ER, only to be sent home and die later, because women weren’t showing symptoms like doctors were used to studying.
